## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh…

AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue

The `TransientRetryNotice` contract documents `attempt` as **"the 1-based attempt that just failed"**. The CLI renders `attempt + 1`.

- Transport path: `_pauseBetweenAttempts(..., state.attemptLog.length, maxAttempts, ...)` — passes the count of failed attempts, so attempt = number of failed attempts. Render shows `attempt+1` = upcoming attempt number. E.g. after 1 failed attempt: attempt=1, display "attempt 2/3".

Wait — but there's a subtlety. Let's think about what `attempt` means and the record.

Transport path passes `state.attemptLog.length` (number of failed attempts so far). ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration). Since gh…

### Thread 1 — BLOCKING: off-by-one

  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads

Fixed in `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` (`_afterRateLimitFailure`): the notice now receives `state.rateLimitRetries` — the 1-based attempt that **just failed**, matching the `TransientRetryNotice` contract and the transport path's convention. The faces render `attempt + 1`, so a 3×429 chain now displays `attempt 2/4 → 3/4 → 4/4` and fa.log (`attempt=${attempt + 1}/$maxAttempts`) agrees; no more `attempt 5/4` beyond the budget.

All three surfaces now tell one story:

- `[net]` line / fa.log: `attempt 2/4` on the first retry (was `3/4`);
- `429_retry` record: `attempt: 1` — the contract value ("the 1-based attempt that just failed"); the record's doc comment (`rateLimitRetryRecordType` + `_recordRateLimitRetry`) now states this convention.

- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — "the notice speaks the FAILED attempt (1/4, 2/4, 3/4)": pins the notice args `[1, 2, 3]` with max `1 + maxRateLimitRetries` (RED before the fix: `[2, 3, 4]`).
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — the record expectation aligned to `data['attempt'] == 1` (RED before: 2).

{"content":"## Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice is off by one

Fixed in `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` (`_afterRateLimitFailure`): the notice now receives `state.rateLimitRetries` — the 1-based attempt that **just failed**, matching the `TransientRetryNotice` contract and the transport path's convention. The faces render `attempt + 1`, so a 3×429 chain now displays `attempt 2/4 → 3/4 → 4/4` and fa.log (`attempt=${attempt + 1}/$maxAttempts`) agrees; no more `attempt 5/4` beyond the budget.

All three surfaces now tell one story:

- `[net]` line / fa.log: `attempt 2/4` on the first retry (was `3/4`);
- `429_retry` record: `attempt: 1` — the contract value ("the 1-based attempt that just failed"); the record's doc comment (`rateLimitRetryRecordType` + `_recordRateLimitRetry`) now states this convention.

Tests:

- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — "the notice speaks the FAILED attempt (1/4, 2/4, 3/4)": pins the notice args `[1, 2, 3]` with max `1 + maxRateLimitRetries` (RED before the fix: `[2, 3, 4]`).
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — the record expectation aligned to `data['attempt'] == 1` (RED before: 2).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"## Thread 2 — rate-limit retries erode the transport budget via the shared `attemptLog`

Fixed with the reviewer's first option: a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter beside `rateLimitRetries` in `_DriveState` (`lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`).

- The transport bound and the transport notice now read `state.transportAttempts` (pre-commit failures, zero-byte watchdog kills, and mid-answer resume attempts — everything the `maxAttempts` budget governs), never the shared `attemptLog` whose length mixes both classes.
- The "must not eat each other's budget" doc at `maxRateLimitRetries` now describes the real mechanism: each class counts its own attempts; the ladder's loop bound (`maxAttempts + maxRateLimitRetries`) stays as the alternation safety net.

Mixed-chain trace from the thread (maxAttempts=3, maxRateLimitRetries=3: 429 → drop → 429 → drop → 429 → drop) now exhausts the transport ladder after its **full 3** transport attempts (terminal on the 6th call), not after 2.

Test: `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — "mixed chain: rate-limit retries do not erode the transport budget": asserts 6 calls, 3 rate-limit + 3 transport failures, terminal `Provider call failed after 6` (RED before the fix: the terminal landed on call 4 after only 2 transport attempts).
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"## Thread 3 — `Retry-After` capped at 60s: cap path now tested, wording aligned

The clamp stays (policy: no unbounded sleeps); the two gaps are closed:

- **Test**: `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — "a Retry-After larger than the 60s cap waits the cap — verbatim only up to rateLimitBackoffCap": `retryAfter: 90s`, no deadline → `waits == [rateLimitBackoffCap]` (the exact case from the thread, `retryAfter: 90s → waits == [60s]`).
- **Wording**: "verbatim" claims are now "verbatim up to the cap" everywhere a reader can trust them — the `_afterRateLimitFailure` doc, the `_TransientFailure.retryAfter` field doc, and the AC2 test comment. The in-code "capped at `rateLimitBackoffCap`" phrasing was already honest and stays.

A provider demanding `Retry-After: 300` now provably waits 60s and the test documents that this is deliberate.

{"content":"## Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason

Fixed with the reviewer's first option, truncation is now display-only:

- **Ladder** (`lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart`): `_pauseBetweenAttempts` callers now hand the notice the **untruncated** provider error (`_noticeReason` — keeping the `run-idle watchdog replay of zero-byte request: …` naming for watchdog replays, issue #1121). The per-attempt evidence log keeps its truncated `_replayReason` form, so terminal stories stay bounded.
- **CLI face** (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart`): `matchesRateLimitWording` classifies the full reason; a new `_shortNoticeLine` (first line, 120 chars — mirroring the ladder's log bound) does the display/record/fa.log truncation. A provider line placing "Rate limit"/"429"/"quota" past char 120 is now announced as `[net] rate limited` **and** gets its `429_retry` record.
- The `TransientRetryNotice` contract doc now states `reason` is untruncated and why.

Tests:

- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — "the notice reason carries the UNTRUNCATED provider line": a 429 wording past char 120 arrives at the notice whole (RED before: truncated at 120).
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — end-to-end: a scripted long-line 429 through headless `fa -p` faces `[net] rate limited` and records `429_retry` (RED before: `[net] connection lost`, no record).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_run_notices_test.dart` — pins the display stays bounded (first line of the reason in the transcript).

{"content":"## Thread 6 — a cancelled backoff wait still appended a `429_retry` record

Fixed with the stronger of the two suggested options in `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` (`_pauseBetweenAttempts`): when the sleeper loses the race to a **non-watchdog** cancel, the notice no longer fires at all — no `[net] rate limited` line, no `429_retry` record — because no retry follows; the aborted terminal tells the story. A watchdog fire landing inside the sleep keeps its zero-delay notice (a truthful immediate replay).

`delay_ms: 0` now has exactly one meaning — an immediate replay (watchdog janitor or mid-answer resume) — documented in the record's payload doc (`rateLimitRetryRecordType`) and in `_recordRateLimitRetry`, so post-mortem tooling can trust it.

Test: `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — "a user cancel landing inside the backoff announces NOTHING": a bare `CancelTokenSource.cancel()` inside the backoff ends the ladder with 1 call, zero notices, and an aborted terminal (RED before: the notice fired with `in 0s`, which is what produced the phantom `delay_ms: 0` record row).

# gh-1602 rework — review round 1 (8 threads: 1 BLOCKING + 5 suggestions + 2 no-id records)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice off by one**: `_afterRateLimitFailure` passed `state.rateLimitRetries + 1` (the *upcoming* attempt) as `TransientRetryNotice.attempt`, whose contract is "the 1-based attempt that just failed" — the `[net]` face/fa.log render `attempt + 1`, so the display double-incremented (`attempt 3/4` … `5/4`) and contradicted the `429_retry` record. **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 2 — shared `attemptLog` budget erosion**: the transport bound read the shared log, so in a mixed chain rate-limit retries ate the transport budget (exhausted after 2 of 3 transport attempts). **Fixed** with a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter.
- 💡 **Thread 3 — `Retry-After` cap untested / "verbatim" overstates**: the 60s clamp stays (policy), the cap path now has a test and the wording says "verbatim up to the cap". **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 4 — fourth copy of the terminal-story boilerplate**: **Fixed** with a `_terminalStory` helper + `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` evidence helpers; all four terminal messages byte-identical.
- 💡 **Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason**: **Fixed** — the ladder passes the untruncated provider line; the CLI classifies the full text and truncates display-only.
- 💡 **Thread 6 — cancelled backoff still appended a `429_retry` row**: **Fixed** — a non-watchdog cancel inside the backoff fires no notice (no line, no record); `delay_ms: 0` documented as immediate-replay only.
- Threads 7/8 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (the "Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES" summary and the `dmtools:review-verdict` record) carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; the summary's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed there. The verdict record is marked "do not edit or reply".
- Pre-existing, unrelated (unchanged): `dart test test/cli/` aborts at process exit in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown (`malloc_consolidate` corruption) — reproduced on clean base 92e9392 per the PR notes; all 5 of its tests pass before the abort, and all 428 `test/cli/` tests pass before it.
- AC3 (live re-run of the run7 shard) still needs a bench run; this rework does not change that scope.

## Approach

TDD per finding — every fix landed behind a test that failed against the pre-fix tree (RED run captured: 5 failures across the three gh-1602 files, including the headless face literally printing `[net] connection lost (…) — retrying in 2s (attempt 3/4)` for a rate-limited long line):

1. **Off-by-one**: notice receives `state.rateLimitRetries` (the failed attempt); faces render `attempt + 1`; the `429_retry` record keeps the contract value and its doc says so (`rateLimitRetryRecordType`, `_recordRateLimitRetry`); headless expectation aligned (`data['attempt'] == 1`).
2. **Budget fairness**: `_DriveState.transportAttempts` counts the transport class (pre-commit transport failures, zero-byte watchdog kills, mid-answer resume attempts); the transport bound + notice read their own spend; the loop bound stays `maxAttempts + maxRateLimitRetries` as the alternation net; the "must not eat each other's budget" doc now describes the real mechanism.
3. **Cap test + wording**: `retryAfter: 90s` → `waits == [rateLimitBackoffCap]`; "verbatim" claims in code docs and the AC2 test comment now read "verbatim up to the cap".
4. **Boilerplate**: `_terminalStory(model, attemptLog, startedAt, story)` for the three plain shells; `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` shared by all four (incl. `_resumedExhaustion`).
5. **Full-text classification**: `_noticeReason` hands the notice the untruncated line (watchdog naming preserved); `_shortNoticeLine` in `agent_cli_io.dart` bounds display/record/fa.log only; `matchesRateLimitWording` classifies the whole reason.
6. **Cancelled wait**: `_pauseBetweenAttempts` pushes the aborted terminal without the notice when the sleeper lost to a non-watchdog cancel; watchdog-replay zero-delay notices unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` — notice attempt convention, `transportAttempts` counter, `_noticeReason`, `_pauseBetweenAttempts` cancel path, `_terminalStory`/`_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed`, doc updates (`maxRateLimitRetries`, `rateLimitRetryRecordType`, typedef, `retryAfter` field).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` — classify-then-truncate notice face (`_shortNoticeLine`), record doc comments.
- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — 5 new tests + AC2 comment alignment.
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — record convention (`attempt == 1`) + long-line 429 end-to-end test.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_run_notices_test.dart` — full-reason classification + bounded display pin.
- Concluded the prepared merge of `origin/main` (gh-1603) into `ai/gh-1602` (conflict-free, `git diff --check` clean).

## Test Coverage

- RED-first: the 5 new/updated scenarios failed against the pre-fix tree (off-by-one attempts `[2,3,4]` vs `[1,2,3]`; mixed chain terminal at call 4 vs 6; truncated vs untruncated notice reason; cancelled-wait notice fired vs silent; record `attempt 2` vs `1`; headless long-line face `connection lost` vs `rate limited`).
- Targeted: `test/providers/` + `test/model_roles/` 1119 passed; `test/agent/` + `test/providers/` 1189 passed; `test/cli/` 428 passed (0 failures; the documented pre-existing exit-abort in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown stands, its 5 tests pass).
- `dart analyze lib/ test/`: 57 pre-existing infos, none introduced (count identical on stashed tree); `dart format` clean.

{"content":"# gh-1602 rework — review round 1 (8 threads: 1 BLOCKING + 5 suggestions + 2 no-id records)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice off by one**: `_afterRateLimitFailure` passed `state.rateLimitRetries + 1` (the *upcoming* attempt) as `TransientRetryNotice.attempt`, whose contract is "the 1-based attempt that just failed" — the `[net]` face/fa.log render `attempt + 1`, so the display double-incremented (`attempt 3/4` … `5/4`) and contradicted the `429_retry` record. **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 2 — shared `attemptLog` budget erosion**: the transport bound read the shared log, so in a mixed chain rate-limit retries ate the transport budget (exhausted after 2 of 3 transport attempts). **Fixed** with a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter.
- 💡 **Thread 3 — `Retry-After` cap untested / "verbatim" overstates**: the 60s clamp stays (policy), the cap path now has a test and the wording says "verbatim up to the cap". **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 4 — fourth copy of the terminal-story boilerplate**: **Fixed** with a `_terminalStory` helper + `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` evidence helpers; all four terminal messages byte-identical.
- 💡 **Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason**: **Fixed** — the ladder passes the untruncated provider line; the CLI classifies the full text and truncates display-only.
- 💡 **Thread 6 — cancelled backoff still appended a `429_retry` row**: **Fixed** — a non-watchdog cancel inside the backoff fires no notice (no line, no record); `delay_ms: 0` documented as immediate-replay only.

The verdict record is marked "do not edit or reply".
- Pre-existing, unrelated (unchanged): `dart test test/cli/` aborts at process exit in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown (`malloc_consolidate` corruption) — reproduced on clean base 92e9392 per the PR notes; all 5 of its tests pass before the abort, and all 428 `test/cli/` tests pass before it.

## Approach

TDD per finding — every fix landed behind a test that failed against the pre-fix tree (RED run captured: 5 failures across the three gh-1602 files, including the headless face literally printing `[net] connection lost (…) — retrying in 2s (attempt 3/4)` for a rate-limited long line):

{"content":"# gh-1602 rework — review round 1 (8 threads: 1 BLOCKING + 5 suggestions + 2 no-id records)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice off by one**: `_afterRateLimitFailure` passed `state.rateLimitRetries + 1` (the *upcoming* attempt) as `TransientRetryNotice.attempt`, whose contract is "the 1-based attempt that just failed" — the `[net]` face/fa.log render `attempt + 1`, so the display double-incremented (`attempt 3/4` … `5/4`) and contradicted the `429_retry` record. **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 2 — shared `attemptLog` budget erosion**: the transport bound read the shared log, so in a mixed chain rate-limit retries ate the transport budget (exhausted after 2 of 3 transport attempts). **Fixed** with a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter.
- 💡 **Thread 3 — `Retry-After` cap untested / "verbatim" overstates**: the 60s clamp stays (policy), the cap path now has a test and the wording says "verbatim up to the cap". **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 4 — fourth copy of the terminal-story boilerplate**: **Fixed** with a `_terminalStory` helper + `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` evidence helpers; all four terminal messages byte-identical.
- 💡 **Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason**: **Fixed** — the ladder passes the untruncated provider line; the CLI classifies the full text and truncates display-only.
- 💡 **Thread 6 — cancelled backoff still appended a `429_retry` row**: **Fixed** — a non-watchdog cancel inside the backoff fires no notice (no line, no record); `delay_ms: 0` documented as immediate-replay only.
- Threads 7/8 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (the "Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES" summary and the `dmtools:review-verdict` record) carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; the summary's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed there. The verdict record is marked "do not edit or reply".
- Pre-existing, unrelated (unchanged): `dart test test/cli/` aborts at process exit in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown (`malloc_consolidate` corruption) — reproduced on clean base 92e9392 per the PR notes; all 5 of its tests pass before the abort, and all 428 `test/cli/` tests pass before it.
- AC3 (live re-run of the run7 shard) still needs a bench run; this rework does not change that scope.

## Approach

TDD per finding — every fix landed behind a test that failed against the pre-fix tree (RED run captured: 5 failures across the three gh-1602 files, including the headless face literally printing `[net] connection lost (…) — retrying in 2s (attempt 3/4)` for a rate-limited long line):

1. **Off-by-one**: notice receives `state.rateLimitRetries` (the failed attempt); faces render `attempt + 1`; the `429_retry` record keeps the contract value and its doc says so (`rateLimitRetryRecordType`, `_recordRateLimitRetry`); headless expectation aligned (`data['attempt'] == 1`).
2. **Budget fairness**: `_DriveState.transportAttempts` counts the transport class (pre-commit transport failures, zero-byte watchdog kills, mid-answer resume attempts); the transport bound + notice read their own spend; the loop bound stays `maxAttempts + maxRateLimitRetries` as the alternation net; the "must not eat each other's budget" doc now describes the real mechanism.
3. **Cap test + wording**: `retryAfter: 90s` → `waits == [rateLimitBackoffCap]`; "verbatim" claims in code docs and the AC2 test comment now read "verbatim up to the cap".
4. **Boilerplate**: `_terminalStory(model, attemptLog, startedAt, story)` for the three plain shells; `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` shared by all four (incl. `_resumedExhaustion`).
5. **Full-text classification**: `_noticeReason` hands the notice the untruncated line (watchdog naming preserved); `_shortNoticeLine` in `agent_cli_io.dart` bounds display/record/fa.log only; `matchesRateLimitWording` classifies the whole reason.

{"content":"# gh-1602 rework — review round 1 (8 threads: 1 BLOCKING + 5 suggestions + 2 no-id records)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice off by one**: `_afterRateLimitFailure` passed `state.rateLimitRetries + 1` (the *upcoming* attempt) as `TransientRetryNotice.attempt`, whose contract is "the 1-based attempt that just failed" — the `[net]` face/fa.log render `attempt + 1`, so the display double-incremented (`attempt 3/4` … `5/4`) and contradicted the `429_retry` record. **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 2 — shared `attemptLog` budget erosion**: the transport bound read the shared log, so in a mixed chain rate-limit retries ate the transport budget (exhausted after 2 of 3 transport attempts). **Fixed** with a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter.
- 💡 **Thread 3 — `Retry-After` cap untested / "verbatim" overstates**: the 60s clamp stays (policy), the cap path now has a test and the wording says "verbatim up to the cap". **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 4 — fourth copy of the terminal-story boilerplate**: **Fixed** with a `_terminalStory` helper + `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` evidence helpers; all four terminal messages byte-identical.
- 💡 **Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason**: **Fixed** — the ladder passes the untruncated provider line; the CLI classifies the full text and truncates display-only.
- 💡 **Thread 6 — cancelled backoff still appended a `429_retry` row**: **Fixed** — a non-watchdog cancel inside the backoff fires no notice (no line, no record); `delay_ms: 0` documented as immediate-replay only.
- Threads 7/8 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (the "Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES" summary and the `dmtools:review-verdict` record) carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; the summary's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed there. The verdict record is marked "do not edit or reply".
- Pre-existing, unrelated (unchanged): `dart test test/cli/` aborts at process exit in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown (`malloc_consolidate` corruption) — reproduced on clean base 92e9392 per the PR notes; all 5 of its tests pass before the abort, and all 428 `test/cli/` tests pass before it.
- AC3 (live re-run of the run7 shard) still needs a bench run; this rework does not change that scope.

## Approach

TDD per finding — every fix landed behind a test that failed against the pre-fix tree (RED run captured: 5 failures across the three gh-1602 files, including the headless face literally printing `[net] connection lost (…) — retrying in 2s (attempt 3/4)` for a rate-limited long line):

1. **Off-by-one**: notice receives `state.rateLimitRetries` (the failed attempt); faces render `attempt + 1`; the `429_retry` record keeps the contract value and its doc says so (`rateLimitRetryRecordType`, `_recordRateLimitRetry`); headless expectation aligned (`data['attempt'] == 1`).
2. **Budget fairness**: `_DriveState.transportAttempts` counts the transport class (pre-commit transport failures, zero-byte watchdog kills, mid-answer resume attempts); the transport bound + notice read their own spend; the loop bound stays `maxAttempts + maxRateLimitRetries` as the alternation net; the "must not eat each other's budget" doc now describes the real mechanism.
3. **Cap test + wording**: `retryAfter: 90s` → `waits == [rateLimitBackoffCap]`; "verbatim" claims in code docs and the AC2 test comment now read "verbatim up to the cap".
4. **Boilerplate**: `_terminalStory(model, attemptLog, startedAt, story)` for the three plain shells; `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` shared by all four (incl. `_resumedExhaustion`).
5. **Full-text classification**: `_noticeReason` hands the notice the untruncated line (watchdog naming preserved); `_shortNoticeLine` in `agent_cli_io.dart` bounds display/record/fa.log only; `matchesRateLimitWording` classifies the whole reason.
6. **Cancelled wait**: `_pauseBetweenAttempts` pushes the aborted terminal without the notice when the sleeper lost to a non-watchdog cancel; watchdog-replay zero-delay notices unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` — notice attempt convention, `transportAttempts` counter, `_noticeReason`, `_pauseBetweenAttempts` cancel path, `_terminalStory`/`_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed`, doc updates (`maxRateLimitRetries`, `rateLimitRetryRecordType`, typedef, `retryAfter` field).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` — classify-then-truncate notice face (`_shortNoticeLine`), record doc comments.
- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — 5 new tests + AC2 comment alignment.
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — record convention (`attempt == 1`) + long-line 429 end-to-end test.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_run_notices_test.dart` — full-reason classification + bounded display pin.
- Concluded the prepared merge of `origin/main` (gh-1603) into `ai/gh-1602` (conflict-free, `git diff --check` clean).

## Test Coverage

- RED-first: the 5 new/updated scenarios failed against the pre-fix tree (off-by-one attempts `[2,3,4]` vs `[1,2,3]`; mixed chain terminal at call 4 vs 6; truncated vs untruncated notice reason; cancelled-wait notice fired vs silent; record `attempt 2` vs `1`; headless long-line face `connection lost` vs `rate limited`).

{"content":"# gh-1602 rework — review round 1 (8 threads: 1 BLOCKING + 5 suggestions + 2 no-id records)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice off by one**: `_afterRateLimitFailure` passed `state.rateLimitRetries + 1` (the *upcoming* attempt) as `TransientRetryNotice.attempt`, whose contract is "the 1-based attempt that just failed" — the `[net]` face/fa.log render `attempt + 1`, so the display double-incremented (`attempt 3/4` … `5/4`) and contradicted the `429_retry` record. **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 2 — shared `attemptLog` budget erosion**: the transport bound read the shared log, so in a mixed chain rate-limit retries ate the transport budget (exhausted after 2 of 3 transport attempts). **Fixed** with a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter.
- 💡 **Thread 3 — `Retry-After` cap untested / "verbatim" overstates**: the 60s clamp stays (policy), the cap path now has a test and the wording says "verbatim up to the cap". **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 4 — fourth copy of the terminal-story boilerplate**: **Fixed** with a `_terminalStory` helper + `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` evidence helpers; all four terminal messages byte-identical.
- 💡 **Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason**: **Fixed** — the ladder passes the untruncated provider line; the CLI classifies the full text and truncates display-only.
- 💡 **Thread 6 — cancelled backoff still appended a `429_retry` row**: **Fixed** — a non-watchdog cancel inside the backoff fires no notice (no line, no record); `delay_ms: 0` documented as immediate-replay only.
- Threads 7/8 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (the "Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES" summary and the `dmtools:review-verdict` record) carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; the summary's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed there. The verdict record is marked "do not edit or reply".
- Pre-existing, unrelated (unchanged): `dart test test/cli/` aborts at process exit in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown (`malloc_consolidate` corruption) — reproduced on clean base 92e9392 per the PR notes; all 5 of its tests pass before the abort, and all 428 `test/cli/` tests pass before it.
- AC3 (live re-run of the run7 shard) still needs a bench run; this rework does not change that scope.

## Approach

TDD per finding — every fix landed behind a test that failed against the pre-fix tree (RED run captured: 5 failures across the three gh-1602 files, including the headless face literally printing `[net] connection lost (…) — retrying in 2s (attempt 3/4)` for a rate-limited long line):

1. **Off-by-one**: notice receives `state.rateLimitRetries` (the failed attempt); faces render `attempt + 1`; the `429_retry` record keeps the contract value and its doc says so (`rateLimitRetryRecordType`, `_recordRateLimitRetry`); headless expectation aligned (`data['attempt'] == 1`).
2. **Budget fairness**: `_DriveState.transportAttempts` counts the transport class (pre-commit transport failures, zero-byte watchdog kills, mid-answer resume attempts); the transport bound + notice read their own spend; the loop bound stays `maxAttempts + maxRateLimitRetries` as the alternation net; the "must not eat each other's budget" doc now describes the real mechanism.
3. **Cap test + wording**: `retryAfter: 90s` → `waits == [rateLimitBackoffCap]`; "verbatim" claims in code docs and the AC2 test comment now read "verbatim up to the cap".
4. **Boilerplate**: `_terminalStory(model, attemptLog, startedAt, story)` for the three plain shells; `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` shared by all four (incl. `_resumedExhaustion`).
5. **Full-text classification**: `_noticeReason` hands the notice the untruncated line (watchdog naming preserved); `_shortNoticeLine` in `agent_cli_io.dart` bounds display/record/fa.log only; `matchesRateLimitWording` classifies the whole reason.
6. **Cancelled wait**: `_pauseBetweenAttempts` pushes the aborted terminal without the notice when the sleeper lost to a non-watchdog cancel; watchdog-replay zero-delay notices unchanged.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` — notice attempt convention, `transportAttempts` counter, `_noticeReason`, `_pauseBetweenAttempts` cancel path, `_terminalStory`/`_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed`, doc updates (`maxRateLimitRetries`, `rateLimitRetryRecordType`, typedef, `retryAfter` field).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` — classify-then-truncate notice face (`_shortNoticeLine`), record doc comments.
- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — 5 new tests + AC2 comment alignment.
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — record convention (`attempt == 1`) + long-line 429 end-to-end test.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_run_notices_test.dart` — full-reason classification + bounded display pin.

## Test Coverage

- RED-first: the 5 new/updated scenarios failed against the pre-fix tree (off-by-one attempts `[2,3,4]` vs `[1,2,3]`; mixed chain terminal at call 4 vs 6; truncated vs untruncated notice reason; cancelled-wait notice fired vs silent; record `attempt 2` vs `1`; headless long-line face `connection lost` vs `rate limited`).

{"content":"# gh-1602 rework — review round 1 (8 threads: 1 BLOCKING + 5 suggestions + 2 no-id records)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — rate-limit retry notice off by one**: `_afterRateLimitFailure` passed `state.rateLimitRetries + 1` (the *upcoming* attempt) as `TransientRetryNotice.attempt`, whose contract is "the 1-based attempt that just failed" — the `[net]` face/fa.log render `attempt + 1`, so the display double-incremented (`attempt 3/4` … `5/4`) and contradicted the `429_retry` record. **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 2 — shared `attemptLog` budget erosion**: the transport bound read the shared log, so in a mixed chain rate-limit retries ate the transport budget (exhausted after 2 of 3 transport attempts). **Fixed** with a dedicated `transportAttempts` counter.
- 💡 **Thread 3 — `Retry-After` cap untested / "verbatim" overstates**: the 60s clamp stays (policy), the cap path now has a test and the wording says "verbatim up to the cap". **Fixed.**
- 💡 **Thread 4 — fourth copy of the terminal-story boilerplate**: **Fixed** with a `_terminalStory` helper + `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` evidence helpers; all four terminal messages byte-identical.
- 💡 **Thread 5 — notice classified the 120-char truncated reason**: **Fixed** — the ladder passes the untruncated provider line; the CLI classifies the full text and truncates display-only.
- 💡 **Thread 6 — cancelled backoff still appended a `429_retry` row**: **Fixed** — a non-watchdog cancel inside the backoff fires no notice (no line, no record); `delay_ms: 0` documented as immediate-replay only.
- Threads 7/8 in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (the "Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES" summary and the `dmtools:review-verdict` record) carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId` to reply into; the summary's findings are exactly threads 1–6 and are addressed there. The verdict record is marked "do not edit or reply".
- Pre-existing, unrelated (unchanged): `dart test test/cli/` aborts at process exit in `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` teardown (`malloc_consolidate` corruption) — reproduced on clean base 92e9392 per the PR notes; all 5 of its tests pass before the abort, and all 428 `test/cli/` tests pass before it.
- AC3 (live re-run of the run7 shard) still needs a bench run; this rework does not change that scope.

## Approach

TDD per finding — every fix landed behind a test that failed against the pre-fix tree (RED run captured: 5 failures across the three gh-1602 files, including the headless face literally printing `[net] connection lost (…) — retrying in 2s (attempt 3/4)` for a rate-limited long line):

1. **Off-by-one**: notice receives `state.rateLimitRetries` (the failed attempt); faces render `attempt + 1`; the `429_retry` record keeps the contract value and its doc says so (`rateLimitRetryRecordType`, `_recordRateLimitRetry`); headless expectation aligned (`data['attempt'] == 1`).
2. **Budget fairness**: `_DriveState.transportAttempts` counts the transport class (pre-commit transport failures, zero-byte watchdog kills, mid-answer resume attempts); the transport bound + notice read their own spend; the loop bound stays `maxAttempts + maxRateLimitRetries` as the alternation net; the "must not eat each other's budget" doc now describes the real mechanism.
3. **Cap test + wording**: `retryAfter: 90s` → `waits == [rateLimitBackoffCap]`; "verbatim" claims in code docs and the AC2 test comment now read "verbatim up to the cap".
4. **Boilerplate**: `_terminalStory(model, attemptLog, startedAt, story)` for the three plain shells; `_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed` shared by all four (incl. `_resumedExhaustion`).
5. **Full-text classification**: `_noticeReason` hands the notice the untruncated line (watchdog naming preserved); `_shortNoticeLine` in `agent_cli_io.dart` bounds display/record/fa.log only; `matchesRateLimitWording` classifies the whole reason.
6. **Cancelled wait**: `_pauseBetweenAttempts` pushes the aborted terminal without the notice when the sleeper lost to a non-watchdog cancel; watchdog-replay zero-delay notices unchanged.

- `lib/src/providers/transient_retry_stream.dart` — notice attempt convention, `transportAttempts` counter, `_noticeReason`, `_pauseBetweenAttempts` cancel path, `_terminalStory`/`_storyLog`/`_storyElapsed`, doc updates (`maxRateLimitRetries`, `rateLimitRetryRecordType`, typedef, `retryAfter` field).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_io.dart` — classify-then-truncate notice face (`_shortNoticeLine`), record doc comments.
- `test/providers/gh1602_rate_limit_retry_test.dart` — 5 new tests + AC2 comment alignment.
- `test/cli/gh1602_rate_limit_headless_test.dart` — record convention (`attempt == 1`) + long-line 429 end-to-end test.
